title: Where your work is kept in {name}: this browser, this device, encrypted
description: {name} keeps your tasks, files and settings in this browser, on this device, encrypted, with no server of its own. What can clear them, and how to keep a copy.
answer: In this browser, on this device, encrypted: your tasks, files, memory, settings and keys. There is no {name} server, and no copy anywhere else unless you make one: a backup, or a folder that your cloud drive syncs.
parts: In this browser, on this device

Each browser keeps its own {name}: what you do in Chrome isn’t in Safari, and what you do on your computer isn’t on your phone. So does each browser profile, the desktop app, and a copy of {name} that your organisation serves at its own address.
Every file is sealed with a key made on this device, which never leaves it. With a lock, {name} opens only with your password or passkey.

A private window keeps nothing once it is closed. Clearing this site’s data, or your browser’s history with its cookies and site data, deletes everything here. A browser short of room may clear it too, and Safari may clear a site you haven’t opened for a week, unless it is on the Dock or the home screen.

A backup is one file with all your tasks and files: see {backup}. In Chrome and Edge, on a computer, {sync} keeps a copy in a folder that OneDrive, Dropbox, iCloud Drive or Google Drive syncs, once {name} offers it.
good: {settings} › {data} says how it stands in one line: when the last backup was made, for instance, or {unkept}
{space}, on the same page, shows how much room each part takes, and what can go to make room.
Installing {name} as an app, in Chrome or Edge or on a phone’s home screen, helps the browser keep its data.
A folder of your computer that you open in {name} stays where it is: in Chrome and Edge, {name} changes its files there; in other browsers, it works on a copy.
Your keys are never in a backup, a sync or a share.
Where what you share goes, brain by brain, and every address {name} contacts: {files}.
fixes: Most often they are in another browser, profile or address. See {gone}.
This window is private. Open {name} in an ordinary window to keep your work.
ask: Where is my work kept, and when did I last back it up?
